clue.text: Woman organist goes to a Spanish city

parts.note: Sara is a woman's name
Sir John Goss was a famous organist of St Paul's Cathedral

explanation.surface: A female church musician sets off on a trip to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to' just joins the pieces. SARAGOSSA is the old English spelling of Zaragoza.
explanation.definitionFit: Saragossa is the traditional English name of Zaragoza, a city in Aragon.

clue.text: Still among the topers in Kent?

indicators.note: among says one word sits in the middle of the group of drinkers

parts.note: topers are heavy drinkers, and soaks are drunkards
still, as in 'still more', means even

explanation.surface: A quiet moment at the bar among the drinkers of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENOAKS is a commuter town in the English county of Kent; the question mark marks a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevenoaks is a town located in the county of Kent, so it is one place found there.

explanation.surface: Something prized or mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the old verb to rate, to scold angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rated means assessed at a worth; to rate someone also once meant to berate or scold them.

clue.text: Denied making a profit on port

parts.note: to make a profit is to gain
Port Said is the Egyptian port at the head of the Suez Canal

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit turning a profit at the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsaid means contradicted or refused, a formal synonym of denied.

clue.text: The type of group that gets under your skin ?

explanation.surface: Some groups are irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: A splinter group breaks away from a larger party; a splinter of wood lodges beneath the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakaway faction is called a splinter group, and a sliver of wood that pierces the skin is a splinter.

parts.note: like means as
sets are the divisions of a tennis match played on a court

explanation.surface: Lawsuits over real estate fought out in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court, but the contests are tennis sets; 'featuring' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things of value a person or firm owns, their possessions.

explanation.surface: A scheme to hide money owed to the landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not money to a landlord but a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch is a small plot of ground, and a patch is sewn on to cover a tear.

clue.text: Soft variety of tails of hair ?

definitions.text: Soft variety of tails of hair

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft

indicators.note: a variety of the letters means a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A gentle style of ponytail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges TAILS to LAITS after P; the whole clue also describes braids, which are tails of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Braided strands are tails of hair woven together, a gentle hairstyle.

clue.text: Fossil type of worm I found in commonplace surroundings

indicators.note: the word for commonplace is placed around the other pieces as their surroundings

parts.note: commonplace means trite, hackneyed
a lob or lobworm is a lugworm used as bait

explanation.surface: A fossil worm turns up in very ordinary rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' just joins; LOB and I sit inside TRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods well known as fossils.

clue.text: Bird goes to church ? Get away!

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A chicken wanders into church and is shooed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hence, used alone as an old command, means go away from here.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
a trio is a group of three
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Coins worth three pounds each, made of a chemical salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-pound' looks like a coin's value, but splits into TRIO and L; 'pieces of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitriol is the old name for a metal sulphate such as copper or iron sulphate.

clue.text: Can it match the roar of the breakers?

definitions.text: Can it match the roar of the breakers?

parts.words: Can it match the roar of the breakers?
parts.note: the roar of the breakers is the sea's, and the creature is named for both the sea and a roaring big cat

explanation.surface: Can anything outroar the waves crashing on the beach?
explanation.definitionFit: The marine mammal is a large seal named for its roar and lion-like mane.

parts.note: knots in a string or the joints on a plant stem are points where things are tied or meet

explanation.definitionFit: A node is a knot or swelling, the point where lines or stems join.

parts.note: a servant telling a caller the master is out when he is in is telling a polite lie

explanation.surface: A guess that someone is lying outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The polite fiction a maid tells an unwanted caller is a lie, though in fact the person is out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means absent from home, or declining visitors with a polite excuse.

clue.text: Attributed, like plagiarism, to a journalist

parts.note: like means as
a crib is copied work
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A newspaperman is accused of copying.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe something is to credit it to a source, so ascribed means credited.

parts.note: Walter Scott's Lay of the Last Minstrel addresses Scotland as 'stern and wild, meet nurse for a poetic child'

explanation.surface: Being introduced to a nurse by a man called Scott.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' here is the old adjective meaning fitting, not a verb; the quoted line names the land as a fit nurse for a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia, the Latin name for Scotland, is the country Scott praised in that line.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some falls cannot be stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt, in the old sense, is to walk lamely, as in 'the halt and the lame'.

parts.note: a bird that settles on a branch is a percher

explanation.surface: A pioneer rides into town on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist; read it as a bird settling, and 'on' stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Percheron is a heavy French breed of draught horse.

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
main means strength, as in 'with might and main'

explanation.surface: This fruit might be an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might' looks like a verb but is a noun, strength; 'be' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearmain is an old variety of apple.

clue.text: I learnt five pieces in the break

indicators.note: broken into pieces, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: During a pause someone mastered five compositions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' suggests musical works but signals that I LEARNT and V are shuffled; 'in' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a break or pause between parts of a performance.

parts.note: the last is a shoemaker's form, and the piece shaped on it shares its name with a flatfish

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the final bit of fish on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler shapes the underside of a shoe on a last, and that piece is also a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside of a shoe, made on a cobbler's last, has the same name as a flatfish.

clue.text: As Juno was heard to exhort Jupiter Pluvius, the brute !

indicators.note: was heard says the words are judged by their sound when spoken

parts.note: Jupiter Pluvius is the rain-bringing god, so his wife would urge 'rain, dear'

explanation.surface: Juno nagging her husband, the rain-god, calls him a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Juno is Jupiter's wife, so her exhortation is 'Rain, dear!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reindeer is an animal, and brute is an old word for a beast.

clue.text: Geddes is told to stop inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the words of the phrase before it

explanation.surface: A man named Geddes is ordered to halt within.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something.

indicators.note: enter says one word goes inside the other

parts.note: sops are small concessions given to pacify

explanation.surface: Someone graciously agrees to start making concessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop is to lower oneself, to deign to do something beneath one.

explanation.surface: A dog, or a comrade from Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is an Irish breed of gun dog; the other is a Communist typesetter, a fellow printer in Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish setter is a reddish gun dog, and a Soviet typesetter would be a Communist printer.

explanation.surface: Getting better after a match at court.
explanation.walkthrough: The court is a tennis court, where long exchanges of shots are called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to regain health or strength; in tennis a rally is a long series of returned shots.

clue.text: Manage to return to Holyhead in time

indicators.note: to return means the word for manage is read backwards

parts.note: to cope is to manage
the head of the word Holy is its first letter

explanation.surface: Getting back to the Welsh port of Holyhead in time.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyhead is a ferry port in Wales, but here it means the head of 'Holy'; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a period or era of time.

indicators.note: to make here says the letters are used to build a new word

explanation.surface: Starting to take notes.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the start or beginning of something.

definitions.note: lentigo is a medical term for freckled skin, a mass noun covering freckles

indicators.note: odd says the letters are in an odd order

explanation.surface: Freckles look strange on a man named Nigel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appear' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentigo is the medical name for a freckle or freckled skin.

clue.text: He recommends a 5d. return by the river

indicators.note: return means the letters for 5d. are read backwards

parts.note: five pence in old money, V for five and d for pence
the Iser is a river in Bohemia and Bavaria

explanation.surface: A man advises a cheap fivepenny return ticket along the river.
explanation.walkthrough: '5d.' is five old pence, written V and D, turned to DV; 'by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser is a person who gives counsel and suggestions.

clue.text: Still seen about like Kingsley's work

indicators.note: about says the first word goes around the second

parts.note: still means yet
like means as

explanation.surface: A Kingsley book still seen, about something similar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is a link. Yeast is an 1848 novel by Charles Kingsley.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Kingsley wrote a novel with this title, so it names one of his books.

indicators.note: altered says the letters of the name are changed in order

parts.note: a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: A card reveals that Lord Elgin's weight has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: A singleton is the only card of a suit in a hand at bridge.
